options.interior: Render the effect mainly through interior thought and perception.
options.somatic: Render the effect mainly through body sensation and physical reaction; name the emotion as little as possible.
options.behavioral: Render the effect mainly through action, gesture and what the character does or fails to do.
options.dialogue: Render the effect mainly through what is said, unsaid, or said wrongly.
options.environmental: Render the effect mainly through how the setting is perceived; let description carry the feeling.

options.sudden: The effect arrives abruptly, at an identifiable moment in the passage.
options.creeping: The effect accumulates gradually; the reader should not be able to point to where it began.

options.recognized: The character knows what they are feeling and could name it.
options.unrecognized: The character does not name or understand the feeling; the reader sees more than the character does.
options.denied: The character is actively refusing the feeling; show the effort of refusal.

options.reader: Aim the effect at the reader's experience (suspense, curiosity, anticipation).
options.character: Aim the effect at the character's experience inside the scene.

options.opening: Concentrate the change near the opening of the passage.
options.throughout: Distribute the change across the whole passage.
options.ending: Concentrate the change near the end of the passage; let it land last.
